## 1.3 Logistic regression models

```{r step-025}
# Set loan status as a factor.
dat$loan_st <- as.factor(dat$loan_st)
set.seed(569)
random_order <- order(runif(nrow(dat)))
index_train <- random_order[seq_len(floor(2 * nrow(dat) / 3))]
index_test <- random_order[-seq_along(index_train)]
# Create training set
train <- dat[index_train, ]
# Create test set
test <- dat[index_test, ]
```

```{r step-026}
# Combine data into a list for processing
data_list <- list(dat = dat$loan_st, train = train$loan_st, test = test$loan_st)

# Compute proportions and combine into a data frame
prop <- do.call(rbind, lapply(data_list, function(x) prop.table(table(x))))
colnames(prop) <- c("no defaults", "defaults")
row.names(prop) <- c("dat_prop", "train_prop", "test_prop")
prop
```

### An age-only benchmark

```{r step-027}
# Fitting a simple logistic model.
logi_age <- glm(loan_st ~ age, family = "binomial", data = train)
logi_age
```

```{r step-028}
age_example_18 <- 18
age_example_60 <- 60
beta_age_0 <- unname(coef(logi_age)[["(Intercept)"]])
beta_age_1 <- unname(coef(logi_age)[["age"]])
age_logit_18 <- beta_age_0 + beta_age_1 * age_example_18
age_exp_18 <- exp(age_logit_18)
age_pd_18 <- age_exp_18 / (1 + age_exp_18)
age_logit_60 <- beta_age_0 + beta_age_1 * age_example_60
age_exp_60 <- exp(age_logit_60)
age_pd_60 <- age_exp_60 / (1 + age_exp_60)
age_min_train <- min(train$age, na.rm = TRUE)
age_max_train <- max(train$age, na.rm = TRUE)
age_logit_min_train <- beta_age_0 + beta_age_1 * age_min_train
age_logit_max_train <- beta_age_0 + beta_age_1 * age_max_train
age_pd_min_train <- exp(age_logit_min_train) / (1 + exp(age_logit_min_train))
age_pd_max_train <- exp(age_logit_max_train) / (1 + exp(age_logit_max_train))
age_pd_observed_low <- min(age_pd_min_train, age_pd_max_train)
age_pd_observed_high <- max(age_pd_min_train, age_pd_max_train)
age_pd_observed_width <- age_pd_observed_high - age_pd_observed_low
aic_age <- AIC(logi_age)
```

```{r step-029}
# Define the function for the logistic regression model
logistic_function <- function(age) {
  beta0 <- beta_age_0
  beta1 <- beta_age_1
  p <- exp(beta0 + beta1 * age) / (1 + exp(beta0 + beta1 * age))
  return(p)
}

# Generate a sequence of ages
ages <- seq(-1000, 500, by = 1)

# Apply the logistic function to each age
p_values <- sapply(ages, logistic_function)

age_curve <- ggplot(data.frame(age = ages, p = p_values),
                    aes(x = age, y = p)) +
  geom_line(color = book_plot_colors[["age"]], linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "Age-model predicted default probability")
```

### Figure 1.4 {#result-figure-1-4}

```{r figure-1-4}
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-cap: "Figure 1.4. Sigmoid curve or logistic curve: age model."
age_indicator_data <- data.frame(
  age = c(age_min_train, age_max_train),
  p = c(age_pd_min_train, age_pd_max_train),
  label_x = c(age_min_train + 80, age_max_train + 240),
  label_y = c(
    min(age_pd_min_train + 0.14, 0.95),
    min(age_pd_max_train + 0.36, 0.95)
  ),
  label = c(
    paste0("min age = ", fmt_num(age_min_train, 0), "\np = ", fmt_pct(age_pd_min_train, 2)),
    paste0("max age = ", fmt_num(age_max_train, 0), "\np = ", fmt_pct(age_pd_max_train, 2))
  )
)

age_curve +
  geom_segment(
    data = age_indicator_data,
    aes(x = age, xend = age, y = 0, yend = p),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dotted",
    linewidth = 0.35,
    color = book_plot_colors[["risk"]]
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = age_indicator_data,
    aes(x = min(ages), xend = age, y = p, yend = p),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dotted",
    linewidth = 0.35,
    color = book_plot_colors[["risk"]]
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = age_indicator_data,
    aes(x = age, xend = label_x, y = p, yend = label_y),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dotted",

    color = book_plot_colors[["risk"]]
  ) +
```


### Adding borrower and loan characteristics

```{r step-033}
# Multiple variables in a logistic regression model.
logi_multi <- glm(loan_st ~ age + int + grade + log(l_amnt) + 
                  log(income) , family = "binomial", data = train)
# Obtain significance levels using summary().
summary(logi_multi)
```

```{r step-034}
aic_multi <- AIC(logi_multi)
```

### Interpreting coefficients and odds ratios

```{r step-035}
multi_summary <- summary(logi_multi)$coefficients
multi_beta <- multi_summary[, "Estimate"]
multi_se <- multi_summary[, "Std. Error"]

odds_ratios <- data.frame(
  term = rownames(multi_summary),
  coefficient = multi_beta,
  std_error = multi_se,
  z_value = multi_summary[, "z value"],
  p_value = multi_summary[, "Pr(>|z|)"],
  OR = exp(multi_beta),
  OR_low_95 = exp(multi_beta - 1.96 * multi_se),
  OR_high_95 = exp(multi_beta + 1.96 * multi_se)
)
rownames(odds_ratios) <- odds_ratios$term
odds_ratios$reading <- ifelse(
  odds_ratios$p_value < 0.05 & odds_ratios$OR_low_95 > 1,
  "clear increase in odds",
  ifelse(
    odds_ratios$p_value < 0.05 & odds_ratios$OR_high_95 < 1,
    "clear decrease in odds",
    "unclear at 5%"
  )
)
```

### Table 1.5 {#result-table-1-5}

```{r table-1-5}
grade_terms <- grep("^grade", rownames(odds_ratios), value = TRUE)
grade_significant_terms <- grade_terms[
  odds_ratios[grade_terms, "p_value"] < 0.05
]
grade_significant_labels <- sub("^grade", "", grade_significant_terms)
grade_reference <- if (is.factor(train$grade)) {
  levels(train$grade)[1]
} else {
  sort(unique(train$grade))[1]
}
grade_significant_text <- if (length(grade_significant_labels) > 0) {
  paste(grade_significant_labels, collapse = ", ")
} else {
  "none at this threshold"
}

grade_first_term <- if ("gradeB" %in% grade_terms) "gradeB" else grade_terms[1]
grade_first_label <- sub("^grade", "", grade_first_term)
grade_highest_term <- grade_terms[which.max(odds_ratios[grade_terms, "OR"])]
grade_highest_label <- sub("^grade", "", grade_highest_term)
grade_or_increases <- all(diff(odds_ratios[grade_terms, "OR"]) > 0)

odds_ratio_table <- odds_ratios[odds_ratios$term != "(Intercept)", ]
odds_ratio_table <- data.frame(
  Term = odds_ratio_table$term,
  Coefficient = fmt_num(odds_ratio_table$coefficient, 4),
  `Odds ratio` = fmt_num(odds_ratio_table$OR, 4),
  `95% OR interval` = paste0(
    "[",
    fmt_num(odds_ratio_table$OR_low_95, 4),
    ", ",
    fmt_num(odds_ratio_table$OR_high_95, 4),
    "]"
  ),
  `p-value` = format.pval(odds_ratio_table$p_value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
  Reading = odds_ratio_table$reading,
  check.names = FALSE
)

companion_kable(
  odds_ratio_table,
  caption = "Coefficient and odds-ratio interpretation for `logi_multi`.",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## 1.4 Predicted probabilities and cutoff rules

```{r step-041}
# Locate the same applicant by the original file row.
john_doe_index <- match("6", rownames(test))
John_Doe <- as.data.frame(test[john_doe_index, ])
John_Doe
```

```{r step-042}
# List of models
models <- list("logi_age" = logi_age, "logi_int" = logi_int, "logi_multi" = logi_multi)

# Estimate the default probability for John Doe using all models
pred_John <- sapply(models, predict, newdata = John_Doe, type = "response")

# Convert to a table with appropriate column name
pred_John <- as.data.frame(pred_John)
colnames(pred_John) <- "Predicted default probability for John Doe."

# Display the predictions
pred_John
```

### Comparing predicted probability distributions

```{r step-043}
# Estimate default probabilities with the three baseline models.
pred_logi_age <- predict(logi_age, newdata = test, type = "response")
pred_logi_int <- predict(logi_int, newdata = test, type = "response")
pred_logi_multi <- predict(logi_multi, newdata = test,
                           type = "response")

pred_range <- rbind("logi_age" = range(pred_logi_age),
                     "logi_int" = range(pred_logi_int),
                     "logi_multi" = range(pred_logi_multi))
aic <- rbind(logi_age$aic, logi_int$aic, logi_multi$aic)
pred_range <- cbind(pred_range, aic)
colnames(pred_range) <- c("min(predicted PD)", "max(predicted PD)", "AIC")
pred_range
```

### From the full-model score to a default probability

```{r step-053}
# Loan status predictions for all test set elements.
pred_logi_full <- predict(logi_full, newdata = test, type = "response")
range(pred_logi_full)
```

```{r step-054}
full_score_test <- as.numeric(predict(logi_full, newdata = test, type = "link"))
full_score_min_test <- min(full_score_test, na.rm = TRUE)
full_score_max_test <- max(full_score_test, na.rm = TRUE)
full_pd_min_test <- plogis(full_score_min_test)
full_pd_max_test <- plogis(full_score_max_test)
full_pd_range_test <- full_pd_max_test - full_pd_min_test
full_score_max_exp <- exp(full_score_max_test)

full_score_axis_min <- floor(min(full_score_min_test, -8))
full_score_axis_max <- ceiling(max(full_score_max_test, 8))
full_score_curve <- seq(full_score_axis_min, full_score_axis_max, length.out = 1000)
full_score_curve_data <- data.frame(
  score = full_score_curve,
  p = plogis(full_score_curve)
)

full_score_plot <- ggplot(full_score_curve_data, aes(x = score, y = p)) +
  geom_line(color = book_plot_colors[["primary"]], linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Full-model score (logit)",
       y = "Full-model predicted default probability")
```

```{r step-055}
full_score_width <- full_score_axis_max - full_score_axis_min
full_score_indicator_data <- data.frame(
  score = c(full_score_min_test, full_score_max_test),
  p = c(full_pd_min_test, full_pd_max_test),
  label_x = c(
    full_score_axis_min + 0.20 * full_score_width,
    full_score_axis_min + 0.80 * full_score_width
  ),
  label_y = c(
    0.30,
    0.55
  ),
  label = c(
    paste0("min score = ", fmt_num(full_score_min_test, 2), "\np = ", fmt_pct(full_pd_min_test, 2)),
    paste0("max score = ", fmt_num(full_score_max_test, 2), "\np = ", fmt_pct(full_pd_max_test, 2))
  )
)
```

### Figure 1.9 {#result-figure-1-9}

```{r figure-1-9}
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 3.6

  ) +
  geom_label(
```

## 1.6 Acceptance strategy and model comparison

```{r step-096}
bank <- function(prob_of_default, actual_default) {
  actual_default <- as.numeric(as.character(actual_default))

  # Pre-define the acceptance rates
  accept_rate <- seq(1, 0, by = -0.05)
  
  # Calculate cutoffs for each acceptance rate
  cutoff <- quantile(prob_of_default, accept_rate)
  # A target of zero rejects every application, including the lowest PD.
  cutoff[accept_rate == 0] <- -Inf
  
  # Calculate bad rates for each cutoff
  bad_rate <- vapply(seq_along(cutoff), function(i) {
    if (accept_rate[i] == 0) return(NA_real_)
    accepted <- prob_of_default <= cutoff[i]
    mean(actual_default[accepted] == 1)
  }, numeric(1))
  
  # Create the result table
  table <- cbind(
    accept_rate,
    cutoff = round(cutoff, 4),
    bad_rate = round(bad_rate, 4)
  )
  
  return(list(table = table, bad_rate = bad_rate, accept_rate = accept_rate, cutoff = cutoff))
}
```

### Balancing accepted loans and default costs

```{r step-101}
actual_default_strategy <- as.numeric(as.character(test$loan_st))

net_payoff_strategy <- function(prob_of_default, accept_rate,
                                good_loan_payoff = 1,
                                bad_loan_cost = 5) {
  cutoff <- unname(quantile(prob_of_default, accept_rate))
  accept <- prob_of_default <= cutoff
  accepted_good <- sum(actual_default_strategy[accept] == 0)
  accepted_defaults <- sum(actual_default_strategy[accept] == 1)
  accepted <- sum(accept)
  net_payoff <- accepted_good * good_loan_payoff -
    accepted_defaults * bad_loan_cost

  data.frame(
    accept_rate = accept_rate,
    cutoff = cutoff,
    accepted = accepted,
    accepted_good = accepted_good,
    accepted_defaults = accepted_defaults,
    bad_rate = accepted_defaults / accepted,
    net_payoff = net_payoff
  )
}

acceptance_grid <- c(0.50, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90)
net_payoff_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(acceptance_grid, net_payoff_strategy,
         prob_of_default = pred_logi_full)
)

best_net_payoff_row <- net_payoff_results[
  which.max(net_payoff_results$net_payoff),
]
```

```{r step-110}
# Calculate ROC curves

roc_to_df_logistic <- function(roc_object, model_name) {
  data.frame(
    false_positive_rate = 1 - roc_object$specificities,
    true_positive_rate = roc_object$sensitivities,
    model = model_name,
    auc = as.numeric(auc(roc_object))
  )
}

roc_logistic_comparison <- bind_rows(
  roc_to_df_logistic(ROC_logi_full, "logi_full"),
  roc_to_df_logistic(ROC_logi_age, "logi_age")
) |>
  mutate(
    model_label = paste0(model, " (AUC = ", fmt_num(auc, 4), ")"),
    model_label = factor(model_label, levels = unique(model_label))
  ) |>
  arrange(model_label, false_positive_rate)

roc_comparison_plot <- ggplot(
  roc_logistic_comparison,
  aes(x = 1 - false_positive_rate, y = true_positive_rate, color = model_label)

    linewidth = 0.35
```

### Measuring probability errors with the Brier score

```{r step-118}
brier_score <- function(actual, predicted_probability) {
  mean((predicted_probability - actual)^2)
}

actual_default <- as.numeric(as.character(test$loan_st))
constant_pd <- rep(mean(actual_default), length(actual_default))

brier_results <- data.frame(
  model = c("logi_full", "logi_age", "constant default rate"),
  brier_score = c(
    brier_score(actual_default, pred_logi_full),
    brier_score(actual_default, pred_logi_age),
    brier_score(actual_default, constant_pd)
  )
)

baseline_brier <- brier_results$brier_score[
  brier_results$model == "constant default rate"
]
brier_results$brier_skill <- 1 - brier_results$brier_score / baseline_brier
```

### Comparing lending policies on the ROC curve

```{r step-120}
# Calculate sensitivity and specificity from a confusion matrix.
classification_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {
  cm <- table(
    Actual = factor(actual, levels = c("0", "1")),
    Predicted = factor(predicted, levels = c(0, 1))
  )
  tn <- cm["0", "0"]
  fp <- cm["0", "1"]
  fn <- cm["1", "0"]
  tp <- cm["1", "1"]
  c(
    sensitivity = as.numeric(tp / (tp + fn)),
    specificity = as.numeric(tn / (tn + fp))
  )
}

# Cutoffs implied by target acceptance rates.
cutoff_full_80 <- unname(quantile(pred_logi_full, probs = 0.80))
cutoff_age_80 <- unname(quantile(pred_logi_age, probs = 0.80))
cutoff_full_65 <- unname(quantile(pred_logi_full, probs = 0.65))
cutoff_age_65 <- unname(quantile(pred_logi_age, probs = 0.65))

# Binary predictions: 1 = reject as predicted default, 0 = accept.
pred_full_80 <- ifelse(pred_logi_full > cutoff_full_80, 1, 0)
pred_age_80 <- ifelse(pred_logi_age > cutoff_age_80, 1, 0)
pred_full_65 <- ifelse(pred_logi_full > cutoff_full_65, 1, 0)
pred_age_65 <- ifelse(pred_logi_age > cutoff_age_65, 1, 0)

metrics_full_80 <- classification_metrics(test$loan_st, pred_full_80)
metrics_age_80 <- classification_metrics(test$loan_st, pred_age_80)
metrics_full_65 <- classification_metrics(test$loan_st, pred_full_65)
metrics_age_65 <- classification_metrics(test$loan_st, pred_age_65)

# Combine the results.
results_df <- data.frame(
  Model = c("logi_full", "logi_age", "logi_full", "logi_age"),
  Policy = c("Accept about 80%", "Accept about 80%",
             "Accept about 65%", "Accept about 65%"),
  Accepted_in_test_set = c(mean(pred_full_80 == 0),
                           mean(pred_age_80 == 0),
                           mean(pred_full_65 == 0),
                           mean(pred_age_65 == 0)),
  PD_cutoff = c(cutoff_full_80, cutoff_age_80,
                cutoff_full_65, cutoff_age_65),
  Sensitivity = c(metrics_full_80["sensitivity"],
                  metrics_age_80["sensitivity"],
                  metrics_full_65["sensitivity"],
                  metrics_age_65["sensitivity"]),
  Specificity = c(metrics_full_80["specificity"],
                  metrics_age_80["specificity"],
                  metrics_full_65["specificity"],
                  metrics_age_65["specificity"])
)
```

```{r step-125}
sens_65 <- as.numeric(tp_65 / (tp_65 + fn_65))
spec_65 <- as.numeric(tn_65 / (tn_65 + fp_65))

cm_full_65
```

### Random and perfect ranking benchmarks

```{r step-126}
set.seed(2020)
random_score_rows <- sort(as.integer(rownames(test)))
random_scores <- setNames(runif(nrow(test)), random_score_rows)
pred_rand_model <- unname(random_scores[rownames(test)])
ROC_rand <- roc(test$loan_st, pred_rand_model, quiet = TRUE)
auc_rand <- as.numeric(auc(ROC_rand))

roc_rand_df <- roc_to_df_logistic(ROC_rand, "Random score") |>
  arrange(false_positive_rate)

random_roc_plot <- ggplot(roc_rand_df, aes(x = 1 - false_positive_rate, y = true_positive_rate)) +
  annotate("segment", x = 1, y = 0, xend = 0, yend = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = book_plot_colors[["reference"]],
    linewidth = 0.35
  ) +
  geom_line(color = book_plot_colors[["risk"]], linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Specificity",
       y = "Sensitivity") +
  coord_equal()

c(random_score_auc = round(auc_rand, 4))
```

```{r step-128}
pred_perfect_model <- as.numeric(as.character(test$loan_st))
ROC_perfect <- roc(test$loan_st, pred_perfect_model, quiet = TRUE)
auc_perfect <- as.numeric(auc(ROC_perfect))

roc_perfect_df <- data.frame(
  false_positive_rate = c(0, 0, 1),
  true_positive_rate = c(0, 1, 1)
)

perfect_roc_plot <- ggplot(roc_perfect_df, aes(x = 1 - false_positive_rate, y = true_positive_rate)) +
  annotate("segment", x = 1, y = 0, xend = 0, yend = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = book_plot_colors[["reference"]],
    linewidth = 0.35
  ) +
  geom_path(color = book_plot_colors[["primary"]], linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Specificity",

  coord_equal()
```
